Geometric mean and confidence interval

Source: R/gmean.r
ks_geom_mean.Rd

Computes the geometric mean of a numeric vector and an approximate confidence interval based on the Student \(t\)-distribution on the log scale (assuming log-transformed values are approximately normal).

Usage

ks_geom_mean(x, na.rm = TRUE, zero.propagate = FALSE, alpha = 0.05)

Arguments

x

Numeric vector (non-negative values; see Details).

na.rm

Logical. If TRUE, NAs are removed first.

zero.propagate

Logical. If TRUE, the presence of any zero in x forces a geometric mean of 0 (and NA confidence limits). If FALSE, zeros are excluded from the mean (only strictly positive values are used).

alpha

Significance level for the two-sided CI (coverage nominal \(1-\alpha\)). Must lie in \((0, 1)\).

Value

A list with components:

geom.mean

Geometric mean (numeric scalar).

geom.sd

Geometric standard deviation, \(\exp(\mathrm{sd}(\log x))\) on the positive data used (same as common PK notation; NA if not defined).

geom.mean.lcl

Lower limit of the \(100(1-\alpha)\)% CI.

geom.mean.ucl

Upper limit of the \(100(1-\alpha)\)% CI.

Details

The geometric mean of positive values \(x_1,\ldots,x_k\) is \(\exp(\frac{1}{k}\sum_{i=1}^k \log x_i)\).

If zero.propagate = FALSE, only \(x_i > 0\) are used. If there are no positive values, the geometric mean is 0 (all zeros) or NA (empty or invalid input after removing NAs).

Negative values are not allowed: the function returns NaN for geom.mean (and CI components) because the geometric mean is not defined in the reals.

The confidence interval is \(\exp(\bar y \pm t_{1-\alpha/2,\,df}\, s/\sqrt{n})\) where \(y = \log x\) for the positive observations used, \(s\) is the sample SD of \(y\), \(n\) is their count, and \(df = n-1\). For \(n < 2\) the limits are NA.

References

Kirkwood, T. B. (1979). Geometric means and measures of dispersion. Biometrics, 35(4), 908–909.

See also

log, quantile

Examples

x <- abs(rnorm(100,10,5))
ks_geom_mean(x)
#> $geom.mean
#> [1] 8.591955
#> 
#> $geom.sd
#> [1] 2.198938
#> 
#> $geom.mean.lcl
#> [1] 7.348344
#> 
#> $geom.mean.ucl
#> [1] 10.04603
#>
